dossier.overview:
**Game Engine** is a top-level tab in the **Resort Operations Desk** (`npm run admin`, port **9477**). It launches editors that read and write **real game files** in the monorepo: overworld maps, character packages, and (later) audio, config, and playtest utilities.

It is **not** the **Library** tab (site metadata: box art, media, models index). It is **not** the **Workshop** tab (milestones, public docs authoring, ideas, bugs). Game Engine is where you ship assets the C++ game loads at runtime.

sections.title: Operator guide
sections.summary: Open the hub, pick a tool, slide back when done. Character Editor keeps its subprocess running until you end it.

blocks.body:
1. Start the desk: `cd pokemon-resort-page && npm run admin` → **http://127.0.0.1:9477**
2. Click **Game Engine** in the top nav (or open **#/game-engine**).
3. The hub lists every registered tool as a card: preview image, title, and short description.

The card list is driven by `tools/admin/data/game-engine-tools.json` and exposed at `GET /api/game-engine/tools`. Add a manifest entry to ship a new card; no desk code change needed when reusing the `map` or `character` workbench.
Game Engine hub with tool cards. Each card is one click away from the shared right-hand workbench.

blocks.body:
**Open:** click a card. The workbench panel slides in from the right. The hub remains underneath.

**Deep link:** `#/game-engine/{tool-id}` (example: `#/game-engine/maps`, `#/game-engine/characters`). Legacy URLs `#/map-editor` and `#/character-editor` redirect to those slugs.

**Return to hub:** use the workbench back control or press **Escape**. URL returns to `#/game-engine` and the card grid is visible again.

**Map Studio** runs entirely in the desk (Node APIs on port 9477). Closing the workbench does not stop any subprocess.

**Character Editor** starts a **Python subprocess** on port **8789** the first time you open it (or when you click **Start character editor**). Sliding back to the hub **does not** stop it. Click **End editor** in the workbench header to stop the subprocess and free the port.
Map Studio open in the workbench. Saves `.owmap` files under `pokemon-resort/assets/overworld/maps/`.

blocks.body:
**Map Studio** — paint RTPKS tile layers, terrain, collision, props, and spawn on overworld maps. Pair with **What is an .rtpks file?** when binding tile packs.

**Character Editor** — replaced standalone SPMK for day-to-day `.charbin` work inside the desk. Packages land in the game assets tree; the C++ loader reads them without calling SPMK at runtime. Authoring schema and binary layout: **What is a .charbin file?**
Planned Game Engine cards (not committed; order and scope may change):

blocks.html:
Planned toolIntent
Audio browserPer-game-section BGM/SFX preview and assignment
Visual config editorEdit gameplay JSON (render, followers, simulation defaults) without hand-editing raw files
Save reset / playtest utilitiesFast iteration helpers for QA (reset slots, warp to map, spawn test party)

Each new tool needs a manifest row, a preview image under public/media/game_engine/, and either an existing workbench type or a new editor module wired in admin.js.

ProblemTry
Tool card does nothing / blank workbenchHard-refresh the desk tab. Restart npm run admin if the Node process is stuck.
Character Editor will not startFirst-time Python setup (venv + requirements). See DEV-PORTS.md in the monorepo root, section Resort site + admin.
Port 8789 already in useAnother Character Editor or stale subprocess. End editor from the workbench, or stop the process (lsof -nP -iTCP:8789).
Card screenshot looks outdatedReplace PNG/WebP under pokemon-resort-page/public/media/game_engine/ (16∶10, ~640×400). Update the image path in the manifest if you change the filename.
Need another Game Engine toolFollow pokemon-resort-page/tools/admin/docs/adding-game-engine-tools.md.

blocks.caption: Checklist for registering a new tool card
blocks.body:
# Adding a Game Engine tool

1. Add a preview image under `pokemon-resort-page/public/media/game_engine/`.
2. Register the tool in `pokemon-resort-page/tools/admin/data/game-engine-tools.json`.
3. If the tool reuses an existing workbench, set `workbench` to `map` or `character`.
4. If the tool needs a **new** editor, implement the workbench module and wire it in `admin.js`.

**Character Editor first-time setup** (from monorepo root `DEV-PORTS.md`):

```bash
cd pokemon-resort-page/tools/admin/modules/charactereditor
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
```

Then open **Game Engine → Character Editor** and click **Start character editor** if it does not auto-start.

**Ports:** desk **9477**, Character Editor subprocess **8789**. Standalone legacy SPMK remains on **8788** for comparison during migration.
